title: Understanding Currency Markets and Exchange Rate Dynamics
subtitle: How exchange rates are actually determined, and what really moves the rupee against the dollar
description: A macro-first look at how currency markets work and why exchange rates move, built for investors and finance professionals who want the theory and the mechanics, not a trading manual. Starts with how the rupee is actually quoted and priced day to day (spot, forward, RBI reference rate, NSE currency futures), then builds the three classical frameworks economists use to explain exchange rates: purchasing power parity, interest rate parity, and the balance of payments approach. From there it moves into the real-world forces that move the rupee: FPI and FDI flows, the crude oil bill and the current account, and the US dollar index and global risk sentiment. Every concept is anchored to Indian data and events, from RBI intervention and forex reserves to the rupee's slide past 83 to the dollar.

whatYouLearn: Read direct and indirect currency quotes and explain how the rupee's spot, forward and futures rates are actually set
Distinguish fixed, floating and managed float regimes, and place India's own currency regime in that framework
Apply purchasing power parity and interest rate parity to explain why currencies drift and how carry trades work
Use the balance of payments approach to connect the current account and capital account to rupee movements
Identify how FPI flows, FDI, the oil import bill and the US dollar index each push and pull the rupee
Read RBI intervention and forex reserve data as signals of how the central bank manages rupee volatility
